pages.title: 中国K12反馈素养｜反馈知识无分反思｜教师自评｜2025英文公开题文
pages.description: These statements come from a teacher feedback-giving literacy study. For each statement, you may describe an example, a learning need or a question. You can leave any statement unanswered or decline to answer. No ratings, scores, levels or automated judgements are produced. This is a project reflection form, not the original validated questionnaire; the original teacher response anchors and scoring instructions have not been verified. Your perspective does not establish the feedback students actually received. Do not include student names or identifiable work. © The Author(s) 2025 (Cui Kang, Jinyan Huang, Ying Liu, Hua Yin). CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. Original English item text reproduced from Tables 2–3 of https://www.nature.com/articles/s41599-025-04927-4. These are author-created items; no separate restrictive credit line accompanies the tables. Project changes: four standalone unscored reflection forms, optional long-text answers, instructions and independently drafted Simplified Chinese working translations. Neither an author-endorsed digital questionnaire nor a validated Chinese/English standalone scale is claimed. No participant datasets, article layout, images or supplement charts are redistributed.

questions.prompt: K1: I understand the theoretical principles that guide effective feedback.
K2: I understand different feedback strategies and their application.
K3: I am concerned with feeding back relevant research to enhance my teaching practice.
K4: I am familiar with different types of feedback and the purposes for which they are used.
K5: I am aware of the impact of timely and appropriate feedback on student learning outcomes.
K6: I know the importance of feedback being aligned with student learning goals and needs.
K7: I know the importance of developing actionable feedback.
